title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act to extend through 2018 the authority of the Federal Election Commission to impose civil money penalties on the basis of a schedule of penalties established and published by the Commission, to expand such authority to certain other violations, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to extend through December 31, 2018, the authority of the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to impose civil money penalties on the basis of a schedule of penalties it has established and published.

Applies such penalties to violations of qualified campaign contribution and expenditure disclosure requirements.

summary.headline: This law extends the Federal Election Commission's power to fine campaign violators using a published penalty schedule through 2018 and covers certain disclosure violations.
summary.what_it_does: The Federal Election Campaign Act lets the Federal Election Commission (FEC) impose civil money penalties, which are fines, for certain violations. This law extends that fining power, based on a schedule of penalties the FEC has set and published, through December 31, 2018. It also applies these penalties to violations of certain campaign contribution and spending disclosure rules.

who_it_affects.how: They can face FEC fines for violating the covered contribution and expenditure disclosure requirements.

who_it_affects.group: Political committees and other filers subject to FEC disclosure rules
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the covered reporting rules or risk fines under the published penalty schedule.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 26, 2013; the penalty authority runs through December 31, 2018.
